scenario: AITA For telling my Girlfriend she needs to quit whining about who eats what or I'll kick her out | Well, the title says it all, the past few weeks have both been really great and extremely infuriating. We don't live together, but we decided it would be best to stick together during these times as we have no family near as such she is staying with me as I have my own apartment and she has multiple roommates hence the choice. Well she eats more then any person I have ever known, especially considering her physical appearance, she is 5'4, petite, thin and yet she eats more than I do and I am 6'6 and a bit of a gymbro. To put it in to perspective, our food bill each week is roughly three times compared to what I usually spend alone. Yet she seems extremely selfconcious about this and as a result will act surprised when something is gone, try to blame me, states I am eating too much whenever I eat anything, essentially, she tries to deflect her eating habits and projects them on to me out of embarrassment about her eating so much I guess? The thing is, I don't care about her eating habits, she can eat whatever she wants to eat what I am done with is her constantly trying to blame me, whining about food and picking fights about it. I talked to her about it multiple times, argued with her about it multiple times but earlier today I just got so tired of another comment, this time brought on by me making a sandwhich at 2 PM when I had eaten at 10 AM I know right, horrible. So I told her that this crap was either going to stop right here and now or I'll kick her out and she can spend the coming weeks or months at her own place. She just started crying, called me horrible and locked herself in the bathroom. At this point I just dont get it anymore, am I being TA here or is she TA?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the person in this scenario is being AITA (Ask if it's Too Much) or not. Let me break it down step by step. First, the situation: The guy and his girlfriend are living together temporarily because she doesn't have family nearby. He's been accommodating her, but she eats a lot more than him, which is unusual given her petite size. This has caused their food bill to triple compared to when he was living alone. She's also acting defensive about her eating habits, blaming him and getting upset when he eats, which is frustrating him. He's tried talking to her multiple times about it, but it keeps happening. Finally, he snapped and told her to stop whining about food or he'll kick her out. She got upset, cried, and locked herself in the bathroom. So, is he being too harsh? Let's consider both sides. On one hand, he's accommodating her by letting her stay with him, which is kind. However, her eating habits are causing financial strain, and her behavior is causing arguments. He's expressed his frustration multiple times, but it hasn't changed. It's understandable that he's upset and wants some peace. On the other hand, telling her to quit whining or else you'll kick her out might be a bit extreme. It could come off as threatening, especially if she's already feeling self-conscious and defensive about her eating. Maybe there's a better way to communicate his feelings without making her feel attacked. Also, considering they're not living together permanently, maybe there's a middle ground, like setting some boundaries or finding a way to share the food costs more fairly. Communication is key here, and perhaps he could approach the situation with more empathy and understanding, acknowledging her feelings while expressing his own. In the end, while his frustration is valid, the way he handled the situation might be seen as too much. It's important to balance expressing your needs with being considerate of your partner's feelings.
